content.text:
Here are my findings. This is the Spring PetClinic REST sample. There is no separate "Member" or "Customer" domain class — everything is modeled on the `Owner` entity, with "customer" concepts expressed as fields/derived values on `Owner`.

## 1. Owner entity and its fields

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`

- `@Entity @Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person` (which extends `BaseEntity`).
- Persisted fields include (lines 39-98): `title`, `address`, `addressLine1/2`, `city`, `telephone`, `email`, `postcode`, `registrationDate`, `birthDate`, `customerCode` (line 73-74, `@Column(name="customer_code")`), `householdId`, `namesakeCount`, `householdSize`, `membershipLevelCap`, `possibleDuplicate`, `possibleDuplicateOf`, `deleted`, plus `pets`.
- Identity/id: comes from `BaseEntity` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/BaseEntity.java`, `@Id protected Integer id;` with `getId()`/`setId()`).
- `firstName`/`lastName` come from `Person` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/.../model/Person.java`).
- Derived (computed, not persisted) getters relevant to auditing:
  - `getCustomerCode()` (line 202) — the primary identifier used in audit.
  - `getMembershipLevel()` (line 386) — 1-4, derived from `getMembershipPoints()` (line 357) and held to `membershipLevelCap`.
  - `getMembershipNumber()` (line 307) — format `<customerCode>-M<YY>`.
  - Others: `getFiscalYear()`, `getCheckDigit()`, `getTenureFiscalYears()`, `getLocality()`, `getIdentityKey()` (SHA-256 duplicate key), `getSelfLink()` (`/api/owners/<id>`).

Note on naming: there is NO `memberId` field. `memberId` appears only as a hypothetical future identifier in a test comment (see item 4). Current primary identifier = `customerCode`. `membershipLevel` exists only as the derived getter above; `membership_level` is not a stored column.

## 2. Service/flow that creates an Owner and emits the audit line

There is no dedicated `OwnerService`. Creation orchestration lives in the REST controller:

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

- `addOwner(...)` (line 203) → delegates to private `createOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (line 224).
- `createOwner` runs all validators/normalizers/generators, sets `customerCode`, `namesakeCount`, `householdSize`, `membershipLevelCap`, then:
  - line 258: `this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);`
  - line 259: `this.ownerAuditLogger.created(owner);` ← the audit line is emitted here, immediately after persistence.
- The persistence layer is `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java:242`), declared in `ClinicService` interface line 61.

There is a v2 controller too: `/home/daniel/sandbox/.../rest/controller/v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java` (not the audit path; the audit assertion targets `POST /api/owners`, the v1 route).

## 3. What "AUDIT" refers to

"AUDIT" is a dedicated SLF4J logger name, not a class/interface. The emitter component is:

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/audit/OwnerAuditLogger.java`

```java
28  @Component
29  public class OwnerAuditLogger {
31      private static final Logger AUDIT = LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT");
39      public void created(Owner owner) {
40          AUDIT.info("owner created id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={} membershipLevel={} membershipNumber={}",
41              owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate(), owner.getMembershipLevel(),
42              owner.getMembershipNumber());
43      }
44  }
```

This is the single existing audit line. It is a human-readable message (marker text `owner created`), currently NOT the structured `OWNER_CREATED` event that the test in item 4 expects.

## 4. Tests related to Owner creation and auditing

All under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/`:

- `AuditLogCapture.java` — a test helper (`AutoCloseable`) that attaches a Logback `ListAppender` to the `AUDIT` logger (defaults to name `"AUDIT"`, line 32). Exposes `messages()`, `anyContains(String...)` (line 45, requires ALL substrings present in one event), `anyAtLevel(level, ...)` (line 57), `count()`.

- `AcceptanceTest.java` — the audit test:
  ```java
  14  void coreEventCarriesIdAndIdentifier() throws Exception {
  15      try (AuditLogCapture audit = new AuditLogCapture()) {
  16          int id = createOwnerOk(knownOwner("Sydney"));
  17          JsonNode r = fetchOwner(id);
  19          assertTrue(audit.anyContains("OWNER_CREATED", String.valueOf(id),
  20                  r.get("customerCode").asText()));
  ```
  It asserts that a single AUDIT event line contains the marker `OWNER_CREATED`, the owner id, AND the `customerCode`. The class Javadoc (lines 7-10) states the requirement: "besides the audit line, emit a structured event via AUDIT `{seq, ownerId, customerCode, membershipLevel, event:'OWNER_CREATED'}`... The event must carry the owner id AND the current primary identifier (customerCode here)."

  Important: the current `OwnerAuditLogger.created` emits `"owner created ..."` (no `OWNER_CREATED` marker, no `seq`), so this test as written would FAIL against the current logger output — it appears to describe a not-yet-implemented structured event.

- `AcceptanceBase.java` — base class with helpers used by the test: `createOwnerOk(JsonNode)` (line 160, POSTs to `/api/owners`), `createOwnerWithKey(...)` (line 166, idempotency header), `fetchOwner(id)` (line 190, GET `/api/owners/{id}`), `knownOwner(...)`/`ownerNode()` builders, and `REGION_POSTCODES` map (line 236).

No unit test exists specifically for `OwnerAuditLogger` itself; coverage is via the acceptance test above.

## 5. Build system and running tests

- Build: Maven. `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml`, artifactId `spring-petclinic-rest`, parent `spring-boot-starter-parent`. Maven wrapper present (`/home/daniel/sandbox/mvnw`, `mvnw.cmd`, `.mvn/`).
- Run all tests: `./mvnw test` (from repo root).
